paras: The police shooting at Andrew Mills took place in Birmingham, Alabama, at about 11 p.m. on 1 August 1895, when two police officers chased Mills, a Black man described as an escaped convict, and fired four shots at him. None of the shots was reported to have hit him, and he escaped; one officer hurt his knee in a fall during the chase.

According to the Birmingham Age-Herald, Mills, also known as "Dago Bill," was "an escaped convict from Coalburg." Officers Culpepper and Whalen recognized him as he stood at Alley D and Twentieth street, and Culpepper, who the paper said knew him, ordered him to halt.

Mills ran instead of stopping, and Culpepper fired two shots at him during the chase, "thinking to stop him," in the paper's words. While firing, Culpepper fell and injured his knee cap. Whalen then continued the pursuit as far as Seventeenth street and fired two more shots, but Mills got away.
The coverage contains no report that Mills was wounded or recaptured, and no inquiry into the shooting appears in it.

The only known report is a short local item on page 5 of the Birmingham Age-Herald of 2 August 1895, headlined "A Lively Chase" with the deck "Two Police Officers Attempt to Catch an Escaped Convict—Four Shots Fired." The item followed the officers' account, referred to Mills throughout as "the negro," and treated the gunfire as a routine part of an arrest attempt without comment. No other white paper and no Black paper is known to have carried the story.

bases: Two police officers fired four shots at a fleeing Black man they were trying to arrest as an escaped convict; no mob or crowd is mentioned (A1).
One local white paper is the only report, and its account comes from the officers' side (A1).
